Method of Attack: Encrypts files by scrambling filenames and appending .osiris extension
Distributed via spam emails with Excel invoice attachments containing macros
Macros download and execute a renamed DLL installer using Rundll32.exe
Ransom notes displayed with instructions to pay ransom
Attempts to remove Shadow Volume Copies to prevent recovery
Attack Vector: Spam emails with Excel attachments containing malicious macros
Indicators of Compromise: Encrypted files with .osiris extension and scrambled filenames like 11111111--1111--1111--FC8BB0BA--5FE9D9C2B69A.osiris
Ransom notes named DesktopOSIRIS.bmp, DesktopOSIRIS.htm, OSIRIS-[4_numbers].htm
DLL files with non-.dll extensions such as .spe executed via Rundll32.exe
Excel spreadsheet with sheet named Лист1 (Ukrainian/Russian localization)
Spam emails with subject Invoice Inv[random_numbers] and zip attachments named Invoice_Inv[random_numbers].xls
